Paper_name: Self-referencing prioritizes moral character on perceptual matching
Summary: The study investigates whether moral information is prioritized in perceptual processing. Through eleven experiments using geometric shapes associated with moral characters, the authors found a robust prioritization effect for good characters. They tested two competing hypotheses: a general valence-based positivity bias and a self-binding account. The data supported the self-binding account, indicating that self-referencing, rather than other-referencing or general valence, is the fundamental driver of the prioritization effect.
Author: Hu Chuan-Peng, Kaiping Peng, Jie Sui
Conclusion: The main results demonstrate a robust prioritization effect of good moral character in perceptual matching tasks. This effect is driven by self-referencing processes, not by a general positivity bias. The findings indicate an innate connection between morality and the self, showing how humans use self-reference to explore the world and learn morality.
